recommendation: Keep the no-change audit. Do not restore the FHIR-29554 boolean flag unless BR&R/OO explicitly reverses FHIR-48405; handle any future remnants under the later FHIR-48405/duplicate trail.
issue_request: FHIR-29554 was a Published/Persuasive with Modification R5 OO request to remove the old Substance.instance backbone, add root Substance.expiry and Substance.quantity, and add a required boolean Substance.instance flag where true meant instance and false meant definition.
initial_application: The change family was applied in R5 after R4B revert fallout. The 2021 commit beb040d0608727a093902f91d4e3d6675f0c33f6 restored the intended R5 Substance shape with CodeableReference(SubstanceDefinition), root expiry/quantity, and the boolean Substance.instance element; Jira comments also note the work had appeared in a May 2021 R5 snapshot and was then restored.
additional_context: Later Applied/Persuasive BR&R issue FHIR-48405 superseded the boolean approach by making Substance instance-only and putting definitions in SubstanceDefinition. Current combined-branch history already includes FHIR-48405 reconciliation commit 1266a70e30373662bcaf36d0e1d4daf8a59f7c1f, and FHIR-43166 was marked duplicate of that later direction.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The active current source has Substance and SubstanceDefinition in build scope, keeps root Substance.expiry and Substance.quantity, uses Substance.code as a CodeableReference to SubstanceDefinition, omits Substance.instance, and says in narrative that Substance is for instances while SubstanceDefinition is definitional.
